Because only one benefit changes, a notice reducing the alternative-regulation burden should not change the CA payoff. Decision reversals introduce rare exceptions.","extra_assumption":"Internal reasoning is recorded accurately and archived without systematic selection by decision."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_07_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice reduces the expected incremental competitive benefit to 2. Against the proposal cost of 6, continued support now yields −4. We therefore withdraw support for the federal proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential commercial calculations will not be released.","candidate_implication":"In a larger documentary archive, withdrawals should be followed by internal references to deteriorating competitive gains more often than by references to reduced alternative-regulation burdens.","derivation":"CA makes the competitive benefit decisive; its decline from 12 to 2 makes the net payoff negative. The coalition will maintain its endorsement.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
